item.title: Release of the Monetary Policy Report

rating.summary: Bank of Canada Governor Macklem announced a 25 basis point rate hike to 2.5%, the first increase since July 2023, citing a deteriorated inflation outlook driven by persistently high global oil prices and improving economic resilience. CPI inflation is running around 3% and is projected to rise to ~3.5% by year-end, remaining above target through much of 2027. The Governing Council acknowledged elevated uncertainty from Middle East developments and US trade actions, signaling a cautious but potentially further tightening path.
rating.stance_rationale: The decision to hike after a prolonged pause, with inflation projected well above target and a warning that further rate increases may be needed, is clearly hawkish. However, the explicit 'one meeting at a time' guidance, acknowledgment of economic slack, and emphasis on elevated uncertainty temper the hawkishness to a moderate level.
key_quotes: There could be a need to raise the policy rate further, but given the uncertainties, we will proceed carefully.
With elevated inflation expected to last longer and the economy showing resilience, Governing Council agreed that risks to inflation had increased and there was less scope for monetary accommodation.
